publications.label: Original materials · Prof. Dehzangi
publications.title: iEnhancer-2L: a two-layer predictor for identifying enhancers and their strength by pseudo k-tuple nucleotide composition
publications.summary: Two SVM classifiers use DNA sequence counts and structural descriptors to identify enhancers and classify strong versus weak annotations. Its 2,968-sequence benchmark is the foundation reused by the other original methods.
publications.note: Data available; complete author training code not located. The first grouped reconstruction reached 76.21% / 60.98% accuracy. Later training-only block balancing gives words plus summaries 63.14% strength accuracy versus 62.80% for words alone, with an uncertain difference. Exact historical performance remains unreproduced.

publications.label: Original materials · Prof. Dehzangi
publications.title: EnhancerPred: a predictor for discovering enhancers based on the combination and selection of multiple features
publications.summary: Combines position-specific class profiles, nucleotide composition, and three-base sequence counts on the same historical benchmark. It predicts enhancer identity and strong/weak labels.
publications.note: Shared benchmark available; runnable author training code not located. Its own feature-selection supplements are distinct from the supplied iEnhancer-2L supplements. Fit label-dependent profiles and feature selection only within training folds.

publications.label: Original materials · Prof. Dehzangi
publications.title: iEnhancer-EL: identifying enhancers and their strength with ensemble learning approach
publications.summary: Combines selected SVM predictors from 171 candidates. Uses the shared 2,968-sequence benchmark and a 400-sequence independent-test supplement.
publications.note: Data and method documentation available; complete author training code not located. All 100 strong test sequences in the current publisher S4 match training; removing them leaves no strong test class.

publications.label: Original materials · Prof. Dehzangi
publications.title: Improving Enhancer Identification with a Multi-Classifier Stacked Ensemble Model
publications.summary: MCSE-Enhancer combines six sequence-descriptor families and multiple classifiers for enhancer identification. Its inspected public code uses the same 2,968 training and 400 test sequences as our files.
publications.note: Public author notebooks and data are available. The inspected original has incomplete cells, test-label optimization and 100 train/test overlaps; its identity with the code behind the 2023 results is unverified. Our repaired reconstruction excludes the historical test. After the 2-mer versus 3-mer comparison, changing only the 3-mer denominator gave 76.82% accuracy with iLearn and 76.48% with literal Equation 7: −0.34 points, with a paired conditional 95% interval of −0.85 to +0.17. This establishes no clear advantage or equivalence. Original-method ambiguities remain; this is an exploratory repaired reconstruction, not exact published reproduction. The next external plan retains the original 2-mer reconstruction; VISTA cohort independence is not yet verified and no external metrics exist.

publications.label: Reference atlas
publications.title: An expanded registry of candidate cis-regulatory elements
publications.summary: A reference map of candidate regulatory DNA. Our collection uses its human enhancer-like subset to annotate experimental regions.
publications.note: Candidate annotations are not cell-specific functional measurements.

publications.label: Experimental bridge
publications.authors: Agarwal, V., Inoue, F. et al.
publications.title: Massively parallel characterization of transcriptional regulatory elements
publications.summary: The study tested a shared library of 60,000 DNA constructs in HepG2, K562, and WTC11 using lentiMPRA. We chose these three because it provides comparable activity measurements for the same DNA in each cell line.
publications.note: Planned use: compare reconstructed model scores with measured activity across cells. Normalization and sequence-independence checks remain required; this comparison has not been run.

Joint-library design and three matching ENCODE experiments

publications.label: Assay comparison
publications.title: Comprehensive evaluation of diverse massively parallel reporter assays to functionally characterize human enhancers genome-wide
publications.summary: A comparison of six K562 datasets examining coverage, processing, orientation, and agreement among reporter assays.
publications.note: Reused source measurements must not be counted as independent validation.

publications.label: Developmental evidence
publications.title: VISTA Enhancer Browser: an updated database of tissue-specific developmental enhancers
publications.summary: A database of developmental reporter experiments with tissue, embryo-stage, sequence, and allelic information.
publications.note: A sequence’s source species and the reporter’s experimental context are distinct. Our stage-e11.5, hZR plan leaves 1,847 candidate fragments after preliminary screening. Independence is not yet verified; there are no external predictions or performance results. Evaluation rules are our design, not a finding of the paper.

publications.label: Regulatory grammar
publications.title: Design principles of cell-state-specific enhancers in hematopoiesis
publications.summary: Synthetic and genomic enhancer measurements provide a controlled route to studying motif combinations across blood-cell states.
publications.note: A later extension on designed motif combinations, with its own import and grouped evaluation.

publications.label: Sequence model
publications.title: Genomic language model for predicting enhancers and their allele-specific activity in the human genome
publications.summary: DNABERT-Enhancer uses DNA sequence representations to predict enhancer annotations and investigate candidate variant effects.
publications.note: Prediction probabilities and measured reporter activity answer different questions.

publications.label: Regulatory prediction
publications.title: Advancing regulatory variant effect prediction with AlphaGenome
publications.summary: A sequence model connecting long genomic context to predictions across gene regulation, chromatin, expression, and splicing.
publications.note: An optional tool for focused interpretation after the experimental analysis.

publications.label: Preprint
publications.title: AlphaGenome Atlas: in silico mutagenesis of the entire human genome improves prioritization and interpretation of non-coding variants
publications.summary: A genome-wide resource of predicted variant effects and derived annotations for prioritization and interpretation.
publications.note: The project includes the paper and supplements, not a copy of the full Atlas.

resources.title: ENCODE4 / SCREEN
resources.description: Human enhancer-like cCRE intervals, the registry paper, and supplementary materials.
resources.use: Compare legacy regions and experimental inserts with modern candidate annotations after verifying genome assembly.
resources.limit: Outside the ELS subset does not mean experimentally inactive.

resources.title: ENCODE lentiMPRA
resources.description: Processed files for eight experiments, including the three joint-library experiments from Agarwal, Inoue et al. (Nature, 2025), plus design and activity tables.
resources.use: Use the shared DNA library in HepG2, K562, and WTC11 to test whether reconstructed predictions agree with activity in each cell. These three were chosen because the study tested the same sequences in all three.
resources.limit: Use the combined TSV or the three replicate TSVs per experiment, not both. Barcode coverage recovers 55,977 specificity-table names; the numerical scores remain unreproduced and two control aliases need original FASTA confirmation.

resources.title: MPRA / STARR-seq comparison
resources.description: Author-reported calls, uniform processing, QC, reference resources, paper, and analysis code.
resources.use: Test whether relationships between legacy predictions and activity persist across independently measured K562 assays.
resources.limit: All six compressed archives are local, including the optional large bundles. Establish shared tested regions and reused source measurements before estimating agreement; the raw archive contains count/metadata files, not FASTQ.

resources.title: VISTA Enhancer Browser
resources.description: Eleven official data and dictionary files, together with the database publication.
resources.use: Planned external evaluation of the repaired reconstruction before the lentiMPRA study. Preliminary screening leaves 1,847 candidates.
resources.limit: Independence not yet verified. Genomic, similarity, family and lentiMPRA-design checks remain; no external predictions or metrics.

resources.title: Hematopoiesis MPRA
resources.description: Processed R data, published and preprint versions, supplementary tables, and author code.
resources.use: Explore whether sequence features capture designed motif combinations and differences between cell states.
resources.limit: Synthetic designs and processing scales require a dedicated ingestion and control analysis.

resources.title: DNABERT-Enhancer
resources.description: Publication versions, supplementary material, source snapshot, and trained-model archive.
resources.use: Compare a modern predictor with reproduced classical features after validating inference and training-data independence.
resources.limit: The model archive is local, but the archived prediction launcher calls a missing Python file. Repair and validate the runtime and checkpoint, and define an independent evaluation set; the local legacy test positives overlap development data.

resources.title: AlphaGenome & Atlas
resources.description: Two distinct works, supplementary files, and an AlphaGenome research-code snapshot.
resources.use: Later examine longer genomic context for correctly mapped regions or variants.
resources.limit: Predictions are not experimental confirmation. The full Atlas is not stored in this project.
